subject.title: feat(telegram): send voice typing cue before transcription

question: Should this PR remain blocked until redacted live Telegram proof shows the direct voice typing cue in a real client, or should maintainers accept source-ordering tests as sufficient for this visible transport change?
rationale: The Telegram scoped review standard asks for real Telegram proof for transport-visible behavior, and the current evidence only proves mocked/source ordering; accepting that gap is a maintainer proof-risk decision.

options.title: Require live Telegram proof
options.body: Keep the PR open until a maintainer-authorized Mantis run, redacted Telegram Desktop recording, bot log, or equivalent live output shows the cue before transcription or the agent reply.

options.title: Accept source-ordering proof
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally merge based on the focused ordering tests, owning the risk that Telegram clients still do not visibly show the cue soon enough.

options.title: Pause until refresh and proof
options.body: Leave the PR paired with the canonical issue while the contributor rebases the dirty branch and supplies live proof.

recommendation.title: Require live Telegram proof
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open until a maintainer-authorized Mantis run, redacted Telegram Desktop recording, bot log, or equivalent live output shows the cue before transcription or the agent reply.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has recent Telegram context-runtime history and is a strong routing candidate for whether source-ordering proof is enough for this Telegram behavior.
